subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should archive recovery for reset transcripts be solved as the open read-only `includeFamily` history API, as a mutable restore/re-index utility, or as both with separate safety gates?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent contract changes model-facing history visibility, sensitive transcript access, and whether OpenClaw mutates archived session state.

options.title: Prefer read-only family history
options.body: Review and land the bounded `includeFamily` path first, keeping restore/re-index mutation out of core unless users still need a doctor-style recovery tool.

options.title: Add a doctor restore tool
options.body: Design a guarded `openclaw doctor --fix` or CLI repair that restores/re-indexes archives with backups, provenance, and dry-run output.

options.title: Keep manual recovery only
options.body: Decline core restore tooling and leave archive access to docs or external tools while keeping existing latest-archive fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Prefer read-only family history
recommendation.body: Review and land the bounded `includeFamily` path first, keeping restore/re-index mutation out of core unless users still need a doctor-style recovery tool.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commit and release history tie this person to the current reset-archive fallback and gateway session-history surface.
